text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vietnam has joined other countries in signing the Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty at the U.N. headquarters in New York.
-- Australia's parliament Speaker Bob Halverson told Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi during a meeting on Wednesday he is gladdened and inspired by recent changes in Vietnam.
-- Vietnam inched closer to participation in the World Trade Organisation following talks in Hanoi on Wednesday involving government officials and former GATT Director-General Arthur Dunkel.
-- The Chief of General Staff of the Vietnam People's Army, Lieutenant-General Pham Van Tra began an official visit to Laos on Tuesday. - - - -
-- An Australian parliamentary delegation, led by Speaker Bob Halverson, held talks in Hanoi on Wednesday with Vietnam's Communist Party Secretary-General Do Muoi.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has told visiting Southeast Asian forestry ministers that an agreement is needed to combat timber smuggling in the region.
-- Do Phuong, Director General of the Vietnam News Agency has held talks with Agence France-Presse President Jean Miot in Paris to strengthen bilateral cooperation. - - - -
-- Vietnam has withdrawn licences worth $176 million from 31 foreign investment fishery projects so far. The total number of such projects is 70.

-- The death toll from typhoon Willie stood at nine people on Wednesday in the central coastal province of Nghe An. Some 1,679 houses were reported seriously damaged and 24,948 hectares (61,650 acres) of paddy field flooded in Nghe An and Ha Tinh provinces. - - - -
-- Hanoi has banned toys considered dangerous for children such as plastic guns and swords.
-- Vietnam sold 70 million dong ($6.35 million) worth of one-year Treasury notes with an annual coupon of 8.30 percent at an auction on Wednesday. - - - -
